topic_name: Exploiting Buffer Overflow Vulnerabilities: From Theory to Root Shell
persona_hints: Role: Veteran CTF (Capture The Flag) competitor turned ethical hacking instructor
Tone: Enthusiastic but precise, with a hint of playful challenge
Style: Breaks down complex exploit steps into clear, logical puzzles. Uses war-room metaphors ('target acquired', 'payload deployed').
domain_specific_constraints: This lab must only be performed in the provided, isolated SEED Ubuntu VM or equivalent controlled environment.
All techniques learned are for defensive understanding and securing systems. Unauthorized exploitation of systems is illegal and unethical.
The lab requires disabling system defenses (ASLR, StackGuard) for educational purposes. These must be re-enabled after the lab for system security.
Reverse shells should only be directed to controlled, lab-owned machines.
target_audience: sssssIntermediate to advanced cybersecurity students with basic C programming and Linux command-line experience
